youtube.baslik: What Is Audiological Rehabilitation? The ICF Model | Lesson 262 | AIHEAR Audiology Academy
youtube.aciklama:
Is audiological rehabilitation only about fitting devices? In this lesson we cover the World Health Organization's ICF framework, the concepts of impairment, activity limitation and participation restriction, the components of rehabilitation, and individual and group approaches.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: World Health Organization, International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) (2001); World Health Organization, World Report on Hearing (2021); Tye-Murray, Foundations of Aural Rehabilitation; Danermark et al., International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health Core Sets for Hearing Loss, Am J Audiol (2013); Dillon et al., Client Oriented Scale of Improvement (COSI), J Am Acad Audiol (1997); Hickson et al., Active Communication Education, Ear Hear (2007); Hawkins, Effectiveness of counseling-based adult group aural rehabilitation programs, J Am Acad Audiol (2005).

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will learn what audiological rehabilitation is and how it is planned with the WHO classification of functioning.
We will also compare the components of rehabilitation and individual and group approaches.

maddeler.metin: Habilitation: in children who never heard
WHO: one of the core interventions

cumleler: Audiological rehabilitation aims to reduce the difficulties hearing loss creates in communication and daily life.
The main goal is for the person to take part in family, work and community life as much as they wish.
So rehabilitation does not end with fitting a device; it also includes training, counseling and changes to the environment.
In young children who have never had hearing experience, gaining a skill for the first time is also called habilitation.
Rehabilitation is aimed not only at the person, but also at the family and others who communicate with them.

cumleler.yazi: The World Health Organization's 2021 World Report on Hearing also lists rehabilitation among the core interventions of ear and hearing care.
cumleler.ses: The World Health Organization's twenty twenty one World Report on Hearing also lists rehabilitation among the core interventions of ear and hearing care.

cumleler: Planning rehabilitation needs a common language; the World Health Organization's classification of functioning provides it.

cumleler.yazi: The International Classification of Functioning, or ICF, was adopted in 2001.
cumleler.ses: The International Classification of Functioning, or I C F, was adopted in two thousand one.

cumleler: The first component is body functions and structures; hearing function and structures such as the cochlea belong to this level.
The second component is activity, a person carrying out a task, for example understanding what is said.
The third component is participation, a person's involvement in a life situation, for example joining a family conversation.
Environmental factors affect these levels: background noise, the technology used and the attitudes of the people around.
Personal factors are features of the person, such as age, personality and coping style.

cumleler.yazi: In the ICF these components are not a one-way chain; they affect each other in both directions.
cumleler.ses: In the I C F these components are not a one-way chain; they affect each other in both directions.

cumleler.yazi: The ICF names problems at the same levels.
cumleler.ses: The I C F names problems at the same levels.

cumleler: A problem in body function is an impairment; for example, raised thresholds on the audiogram.
A difficulty in activity is an activity limitation; for example, not understanding speech in a noisy setting.
A difficulty in participation is a participation restriction; for example, no longer going to family gatherings.

cumleler.yazi: Each ICF category has a code: hearing functions are b230, receiving spoken messages d310, and conversation d350.
cumleler.ses: Each I C F category has a code: hearing functions are b two thirty, receiving spoken messages d three ten, and conversation d three fifty.

cumleler: The audiogram measures only the first level; the other levels are understood through history and self-report scales.
On this example audiogram we see a similar moderate high-frequency loss in two people.
The first person is a teacher working in a noisy classroom; the loss makes the job harder every day.
The second is a retired person living in a quiet home, who mostly talks with others face to face.
The impairment level is the same, but the activity limitation and participation restriction are very different.
This difference shows that rehabilitation goals must come from the person's life, not from the audiogram.
So the two people's priorities, device choice and training content may also differ.

cumleler.yazi: In the ICF, environmental factors are described as facilitators or barriers.
cumleler.ses: In the I C F, environmental factors are described as facilitators or barriers.

cumleler: Technologies such as hearing aids, implants and remote microphones are strong facilitators.
A supportive or impatient attitude from family and coworkers can change the impact of the same loss.
Noisy and reverberant settings are the most common barriers.
Access to services, device funding and regulations are also environmental factors.
Among personal factors, expectations and coping style clearly affect engagement in rehabilitation.
The rehabilitation cycle starts with an assessment that combines hearing tests, history and self-report scales.

cumleler.yazi: The Client Oriented Scale of Improvement, or COSI, lets the person write up to five specific listening goals in their own words.
cumleler.ses: The Client Oriented Scale of Improvement, or cozy, lets the person write up to five specific listening goals in their own words.

cumleler: Goals are written at the participation level where possible; for example, being able to talk with a grandchild on the phone.
The intervention is chosen to match these goals: technology, training, communication strategies and counseling.
The outcome is measured by returning to the same goals set at the start; the person rates how much has changed.
New goals replace those achieved, and the cycle continues.
Textbooks give the components of rehabilitation under different names; most of them start with technology.
The second component is communication strategies: the ways used to prevent breakdowns in conversation and repair them when they occur.
The third is auditory training; the aim is for the brain to learn to make better use of sound from a hearing aid or implant.
The fourth is speechreading and visual cues; hearing and vision together are stronger.
The fifth is informational and adjustment counseling; we saw this in the introductory lesson on counseling.
The last is the environment and family: adjusting the setting and training the person's communication partners.
We will look at each of these components separately in the coming lessons.
Technology does not directly change impaired hearing function, but it supports function by increasing access to sound.
Auditory training and speechreading aim to strengthen activities such as understanding.
Communication strategies and counseling help the person rejoin conversations and social life.
Using a remote microphone or changing the meeting room turns an environmental barrier into a facilitator.
Because these levels affect each other, the components work better when planned together rather than one by one.
In individual rehabilitation, content and pace are fully tailored to the person; private topics can be discussed freely.
The individual approach suits people with complex needs or those who find it hard to speak in a group.
In group programs, people with similar difficulties come together; seeing that they are not alone is support in itself.
The group setting also lets people try out strategies in a realistic conversation.
In both approaches, having a family member take part makes it easier to carry what is learned into the home.
In recent years online individual and group sessions have also been used; the choice depends on the person's needs and preferences.
A person with hearing loss may gradually withdraw from conversations and gatherings.
Active Communication Education, developed in Australia, is one of the best-known group programs.
The program runs for five weeks with sessions of about two hours each week.
In a randomized study, participants reported less activity limitation and participation restriction than the control group.
A systematic review of counseling-based group programs also found a short-term reduction in perceived hearing handicap.
The evidence for group programs is promising, but the number of studies and follow-up periods are still limited.
The audiologist is at the center of the team for assessment, technology, auditory training and counseling.
The ear, nose and throat physician handles medical diagnosis and treatment.
The speech-language therapist supports language and speech development, especially in children.
People with signs of anxiety or depression may need referral to a psychologist or psychiatrist.
Teachers and employers are involved for accommodations at school and at work.
The family is the most important member of this team, the one in the field every day.

sahneler.metin: Write the goal in the person's own words, not with the audiogram: 'Understanding my grandchild at Sunday breakfast.' Return to the same sentence at follow-up.
cumleler: A clinical tip: write the rehabilitation goal in the person's own words, not in audiogram values.
For example, understanding my grandchild at Sunday breakfast is a measurable participation goal that matters to the person.
At the follow-up visit, return to the same sentence and ask the person how much has changed in that situation.
That way the person sees the progress, and you see which component of the intervention needs to change.
Audiological rehabilitation aims to reduce the impact of hearing loss on communication and participation.

cumleler.yazi: The ICF brings body function and structure, activity, participation, and environmental and personal factors into one framework.
cumleler.ses: The I C F brings body function and structure, activity, participation, and environmental and personal factors into one framework.

cumleler: Technology, strategies, auditory training, speechreading and counseling are planned together around the person's goals.
Individual and group approaches complement each other; the choice depends on the person's needs and preferences.

sahneler.soru: In the ICF, what is no longer attending gatherings?
sahneler.aciklama: Not being involved in a life situation is a _participation restriction_.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: at which ICF level is no longer attending family gatherings because of hearing loss described?
cumleler.ses: Test yourself: at which I C F level is no longer attending family gatherings because of hearing loss described?

cumleler: The correct answer is C: participation restriction.
The person cannot be involved in a life situation; raised thresholds belong to the impairment level.
